items.title: Baby’s body found in Kuala Berang drain missing head and hand, police investigating
items.summary: KUALA BERANG, Oct 17 — The body of a baby was found in a drain in a residential area in Kampung Padang Setengge, near here, yesterday evening. Hulu Terengganu district police chief Supt Sharudin Abdul Wahab said police received a report from a member of the public about the discovery at about 6.52pm. He said the D10 forensic unit and K9 unit of the Terengganu contingent police headquarters were called in to assist with investigations and gather evidence at the scene.

items.title: Morocco's new government sworn in under first female prime minister
items.summary: She heads a new government formed by a four-party coalition comprising her Authenticity and Modernity Party, the Istiqlal Party, the Socialist Union of Popular Forces, and the Party of Progress and Socialism. The new government includes seven women, including Fatima Ezzahra, compared with six in the previous government led by Aziz Akhannouch. The new government comprises 32 members, including ministers and ministers-delegate, according to official figures.

items.title: Sabah police: Man critically injured as homemade fish bomb explodes in Manggatal kitchen
items.summary: Kota Kinabalu district police chief ACP Shahrudin Mat Husain said the 37-year-old victim sustained serious injuries to both hands and his abdomen in the incident, which occurred at about 2.15 pm. He said preliminary investigations found that the victim was believed to have been making a homemade explosive device for fishing purposes. Following the incident, the police, together with the Bomb Disposal Unit from the Sabah police contingent headquarters and officers from the Kota Kinabalu district police headquarters, conducted an inspection at the scene.

items.title: Johor wants Asean to call meeting on future preventive measures on cross-border haze
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 17 — The Johor State Government has called on Asean nations to hold an emergency meeting to strengthen fire control and prevention measures as well as hotspot monitoring in the future. Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the matter was discussed during the State-Level Disaster Coordination Meeting, which also focused on the risk of cross-border haze following hotspot activities in Indonesia. He said that Johor has been facing a haze episode since August 25, with several areas recording Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy and very unhealthy levels.

items.title: Johor leads unhealthy air quality readings, followed by Selangor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Johor and Selangor remain the states worst affected by haze, with 24 air quality monitoring stations nationwide recording unhealthy levels as of 8.30am today. Data from the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System showed eight stations in Johor and five in Selangor recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings. Meanwhile, 43 stations nationwide recorded moderate air quality.

items.title: #NSTviral: Malaysian travellers moved as accordionist plays Negaraku in Georgia [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Two Malaysian travellers were in for a surprise when a street accordionist in Tbilisi, Georgia, played Negaraku after learning they were from Malaysia. "Far away in Georgia, I heard Negaraku! @allenyeoh29 Jauh-Jauh Di Georgia, Terdengar Lagu NEGARAKU!

items.title: UN Security Council holds 6th straw poll on secretary-general candidates
items.summary: NEW YORK: The UN Security Council on Friday held its sixth straw poll on candidates vying to become the next UN secretary-general, reported Xinhua. Security Council straw polls on secretary-general candidates are informal closed-door ballots used to determine the viability of the candidates. Through the polls, the Security Council selects a candidate to recommend to the General Assembly for appointment as the next UN secretary-general.

items.title: King graces Royal Mess Night in conjunction with 93rd Armed Forces Day
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia attended the Royal Mess Night in conjunction with the 93rd Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) Day at Wisma Perwira ATM here yesterday. According to a post on the Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar Facebook page, His Majesty was received upon arrival by Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar. Also present were Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail and Auditor-General Datuk Seri Wan Suraya Wan Mohd Radzi.

items.title: ISF venturing into NRW for next growth wave [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Less than a year after its debut on Bursa Malaysia, ISF Group Bhd is looking to further diversify its revenue base with recurring income sources from partnerships with states water authority to reduce non-revenue water (NRW). "ISF is looking at elevating our position to public infra, like projects from PAAB (Perbadanan Aset Air Bhd), and projects from state governments," said its group managing director Jeff Ai Boon Chen in an exclusive interview with Business Times. Because we are looking at the long term, rather than every time we need one-off technology," said Ai.

items.title: Malaysia's GDP growth beats expectations [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's third-quarter 2026 advance gross domestic product (GDP) estimate of 5.3 per cent is a positive surprise despite external shocks, particularly the ongoing US-Iran conflict, economists said. "Overall, it is a positive surprise and it looks like the growth numbers could be surprised on the upside with the prevailing GDP growth projection currently standing between 4.8 per cent to 5.3 per cent," the economist said. He added that growth of 5.3 per cent would put Malaysia's economy above its estimated trend growth rate of around 4.7 per cent.

items.title: Pas' move to prioritise Umno, BN signals intent, not electoral realignment, says analyst
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pas' decision to prioritise Umno and Barisan Nasional in negotiations for the next general election signals a willingness to explore closer cooperation, but does not yet indicate a new electoral alliance is taking shape, says a political analyst. Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Tawfik Yaakub said the decision by Pas' Syura Council gave the party's central leadership room to pursue talks with Umno and BN while potentially strengthening its bargaining position with other political parties. Yesterday, Pas spiritual leader Datuk Hashim Jasin said the party would prioritise Umno and BN over other political parties in negotiations for the next general election .

items.title: N. Korea tests AI-assisted torpedo system: KCNA
items.summary: SEOUL: North Korea has tested a "new-type" precision-guided torpedo system that uses artificial intelligence for target detection and guidance, state news agency KCNA reported early Saturday. "AI technology was applied to the target detection and the guidance function of the new-type super-speed precisely guided torpedo," KCNA said. Analysts have said North Korea could be rapidly advancing its missile technology with Russian military support in exchange for sending troops to support its war against Ukraine.

items.title: Kenya records third Ebola case in the country
items.summary: NAIROBI: Kenya has recorded its third case of Ebola, a close relative of the country's first two Ebola cases, the health ministry said on Friday. Just over a week later a second man, a relative of the first, also tested positive for the virus while in quarantine. The DRC declared its 17th Ebola outbreak in May.

items.title: 'Great hero' praised for saving lives in Oregon school shooting
items.summary: BEND, United States: The "hero" who shot dead a teenage gunman after he had already killed three children and a teacher at an elementary school was named Friday, as the US entered a familiar – and likely fruitless – debate about gun control in the wake of the latest tragedy. Kyle Giamanco said 36-year-old Kaylub, who has two children at the school, was driving home for his lunch break on Thursday when he heard gunshots and saw Griffin going into the special education room of the school. US President Donald Trump hailed Giamanco as a "great hero."

items.title: Transport infrastructure under siege: Cable thieves putting commuters at risk
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Cable thieves continue to target transport infrastructure, with recent incidents involving the Kajang MRT Line and the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) highlighting security concerns. In the latest incident, thieves cut about 100m of cable between Phileo Damansara and Pusat Bandar Damansara stations early yesterday. Separately, PLUS Malaysia Bhd said its personnel and police had foiled a suspected cable theft attempt along the NKVE, leading to a suspect's arrest.

items.title: NST CRIME WATCH: Fatal BYD Seal crash, police chase and cable theft arrests [WATCH]
items.summary: Police said initial investigations found that the BYD Seal had rear-ended the Bezza, triggering a chain collision involving a Yamaha 135LC motorcycle and three other cars – a Nissan Almera, Toyota Alphard and Perodua Myvi. Here are the week's other major crime stories: DRAMATIC POLICE CHASE IN WANGSA MAJU Two men were arrested after a police chase from Bukit Antarabangsa to Setiawangsa on Oct 11. Videos of the pursuit and members of the public helping police went viral on social media.

items.title: NST COURT WATCH: School tragedies, fatal crashes and child abuse [WATCH]
items.summary: In Batu Pahat, a Form 4 student was charged with murdering his classmate, Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, at their school in Yong Peng. In Kuala Lumpur, a 24-year-old motorist denied causing five-year-old Asiah Ahmad Syahir's death through reckless driving. Two other children's deaths also featured in court proceedings.

items.title: King graces Royal Mess Night in conjunction with 93rd Armed Forces Day
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia attended the Royal Mess Night in conjunction with the 93rd Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) Day at Wisma Perwira ATM here yesterday. According to a post on the Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar Facebook page, His Majesty was received upon arrival by Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar. Also present were Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail and Auditor-General Datuk Seri Wan Suraya Wan Mohd Radzi.

items.title: Trump's new press secretary out after less than week
items.summary: WASHINGTON: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia was pushed out Friday after less than a week in the high-profile job, following a series of blunders that added to distractions for her embattled boss President Donald Trump. "Can confirm," a White House official told AFP, after Fox News reported that Zacharia, 41, was "transitioning out." Trump told reporters.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Record RM57bil financing facilities for MSMEs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has allocated a record RM57 billion in financing facilities for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) under the 2027 Budget to help the sector navigate global economic uncertainties. Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim said the allocation, up from RM50 billion previously, reflected the government's commitment to strengthening the sector through better access to financing, lower business costs and improved government service delivery. He said the government understood the pressures MSMEs faced amid global economic fluctuations, including rising energy costs and supply chain disruptions beyond the country's control.

items.title: Man critical after homemade fish bomb explodes in Sabah home
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: A 37-year-old man is in critical condition after a homemade fish bomb exploded in the kitchen of a house in Kampung Keliangau, Manggatal. Kota Kinabalu police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrudin Mat Husain said the victim suffered serious injuries to both hands and his abdomen in the 2.15pm incident. Police, together with the Bomb Disposal Unit from the Sabah police contingent headquarters and officers from the Kota Kinabalu police headquarters inspected the scene.

items.title: Asked if Trump is scapegoating him, Zelenskyy just smiles
items.summary: BRUSSELS: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy gave a knowing smile and remained silent on Friday when asked if Donald Trump was scapegoating him for troubles in the US. "This is my answer," Zelenskyy said, as journalists burst into laughter at a press conference in Brussels after he met EU leaders. "Yesterday was a thousand drones in Ukraine, a thousand, but the American side said that it is difficult to speak with Zelenskyy, it's less difficult to manage with Putin," Zelenskyy said.

items.title: NST Leader: Scrap metal theft: Go after the buyers, too
items.summary: THERE seems to be an almost insatiable demand for scrap metal. It started many years ago. The raging fire in Pasir Gudang, Johor, in recent days is said to be deliberately started by cable thieves seeking to separate scrap metal from piles of wood.

items.title: Two days on the campaign trail, Trump faces fading enthusiasm
items.summary: DONALD Trump is crisscrossing America to drum up votes for Republican candidates facing tough midterm election races, but the United States president's rallies are often hijacked by his basking in the adulation of fervent supporters. Journalists followed him on Tuesday and Wednesday during one such trip out West, a rapid succession of flights and rallies — in a glacial valley in Alaska, on an arid plain in Arizona and in the forests of Montana. The Republican leader is betting on his ability to mobilise voters despite polls predicting that his party will lose control of one or both chambers of Congress on Nov 3.

items.title: Court of Appeal reserves decision in Papagomo's contempt appeal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal three-member panel today reserved its decision on blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris's appeal against the High Court's decision which sentenced him to 30 days in jail for contempt of court in a defamation suit filed by former Inspector-General of Polis Tan Sri Razarudin Husain @ Abd Rasid. On Aug 27, 2025, High Court Judicial Commissioner Gan Techiong ruled that Azri, also known as Papagomo, had breached a court injunction concerning the ongoing defamation suit filed by Razarudin. However, lawyer Raam Kumar representing Razarudin, urged the court to uphold the two contempt orders made by the High Court.

items.title: Italy, Spain agree to remove border checks
items.summary: BRUSSELS: Italy and Spain have agreed to remove tit-for-tat border checks introduced following a spat over migration, after talks between the two countries' leaders, diplomatic and government sources said on Friday. The detente ends a showdown that began in summer, when Italy's interior ministry introduced controls on travellers from Spain after tens of thousands of migrants rushed from Morocco into the Spanish territory of Ceuta, in North Africa. The deal was struck after Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Spain's Pedro Sanchez held talks on the sidelines of the leaders' meeting, where migration was on the agenda, a Spanish diplomat said.

items.title: Singapore to issue notices to seven Indonesian firms over haze
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore will issue preventive measure notices to seven Indonesian companies suspected of contributing to transboundary haze through forest fires, Sustainability and Environment Minister Grace Fu said. She said the notices would be issued by the National Environment Agency (NEA), following investigations into errant companies found responsible for causing transboundary haze in Singapore. Fu said the notices seek the companies to deploy firefighting personnel to extinguish fires on land owned or occupied by them and prevent the fires from spreading.

items.title: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepts missiles, drones over Riyadh, other areas
items.summary: RIYADH: The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Friday that it had intercepted missiles and drones over Riyadh and other areas, as the kingdom came under sustained attack from its Iran-backed foes. Since Yemen's civil war flared up again in July, the Houthis have repeatedly struck Saudi targets, including Red Sea tankers, oil facilities and Riyadh's international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week. Saudi Arabia leads a military coalition that has supported Yemen's internationally recognised government against the Houthis for more than a decade.

items.title: Managing Kuching's thriving private healthcare industry
items.summary: The 200-bed Gleneagles Hospital Kuching will open in 2028 while the Regency Specialist Hospital Kuching is a 300-bed facility scheduled to open in 2029. Private healthcare in Kuching was pioneered by the Normah Medical Specialist Centre some 35 years ago. The KPJ Kuching Specialist Hospital rounds up the presently operating four private hospitals in Kuching.

items.title: Ab Rauf: BN's Melaka candidates ready for announcement
items.summary: MASJID TANAH: Barisan Nasional's (BN) Melaka election candidates have been finalised and could be announced at any time, says state BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. The Melaka chief minister said he would not take long to announce the candidates, with nomination day approaching. "Who said that (Oct 24)?

items.title: NRD: Viral video of Saifuddin solemnising non-Muslim marriage dates back to 2023
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A viral video showing Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail solemnising a civil marriage between a non-Muslim couple was recorded in 2023, the National Registration Department (NRD) said. The department said the video was part of its Diamond Jubilee celebration held in conjunction with National Registration Day that year, and the matter had already been clarified on Oct 25 that year. The department said it was responsible for registering civil marriages between non-Muslim couples under the Law Reform (Marriage and Divorce) Act.

items.title: Anwar wishes Malaysian contingent success at Asian Para Games
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has wished the Malaysian contingent success at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games in Japan from Oct 18 to 24. He expressed hope that the national athletes would demonstrate fighting spirit, courage and determination to give their best at the Games. "The entire Malaysian people stand firmly behind you.

items.title: Baby's body found in drain, missing head and one hand
items.summary: KUALA BERANG: The body of a baby, missing its head and one hand, was found in a drain behind a house in Kampung Padang Setengge here this evening. Hulu Terengganu police chief Superintendent Sharudin Abdul Wahab said police received a report on the discovery at 6.52pm. "The baby's body was found without its head and missing one hand.

items.title: Amanah allocated eight seats for Melaka election
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Amanah has been allocated eight state seats to contest in the Melaka election, subject to final approval by Pakatan Harapan (PH). Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, who is also agriculture and food security minister, said the allocation was the outcome of discussions at the PH level. However, he said the final decision would be made by the PH presidential council on Oct 24.

items.title: Zahid says Malaysia ready to help Indonesia fight forest fires after Prabowo accepts foreign aid
items.summary: TIANJIN, Oct 16 — Malaysia is ready to help Indonesia tackle widespread forest and land fires after President Prabowo Subianto agreed to accept offers of assistance from neighbouring countries. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Malaysia welcomed the Indonesian government’s openness to receiving foreign assistance to fight the fires. “We are grateful to the Indonesian government and President Prabowo for being open to accepting foreign assistance to tackle the forest fires.

items.title: Perlis MACC recovers nearly RM700,000 through forfeitures since 2024
items.summary: ARAU, Oct 16 — The Perlis Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has recovered RM698,255.55 through forfeitures from 2024 to date. Perlis MACC director Mohd Nor Adha Ab Gani said the state anti-graft agency opened 65 investigation papers (IPs), recorded 84 arrests and brought 37 charges to court during the period. Mohd Nor Adha said Perlis MACC also focused on preventive measures, submitting 61 Governance Improvement Recommendations to federal and state departments and statutory bodies.

items.title: El Niño could hit fishermen, fish farms as temperatures soar to 40°C, says Mat Sabu
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 16 — Coastal fishermen and aquaculture operators could be hit if El Niño pushes temperatures up to 40°Celsius, prompting calls for early preparations to protect the country’s food production. Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the phenomenon could drive fish farther out to sea, posing a challenge for coastal fishermen who lack the capacity to fish in deeper waters. He said the government had discussed preparations for El Niño with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim as part of efforts to strengthen national food security.

items.title: Two TNB staff critically injured by electric shock as substation fire triggers Johor Bahru blackout (VIDEO)
items.summary: The incident triggered a fire and disrupted electricity supply in parts of Johor Bahru. TNB said the fire broke out at 6.03pm, interrupting power supply in several areas around Johor Jaya and its surrounding areas. The Johor Fire and Rescue Department said the Tebrau fire station received a distress call about the incident at 6.10pm.

items.title: AAIB flags firefighting gaps at Sarawak airstrip after crash killed five
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Air Accidents Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has urged the operator of Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Port (STOLport) in Miri, Sarawak, to review its rescue and firefighting arrangements after a helicopter crash killed five people, including four Health Ministry personnel, on September 8. The AAIB recommended that aerodrome operator Malaysia Airports Sdn Bhd (MASB) review rescue and firefighting arrangements across its STOLports to ensure auxiliary personnel were properly trained and equipped, and that firefighting equipment and personal protective equipment (PPE) were properly maintained and serviceable. The bureau said the recommendation followed findings that Malaysia Volunteers Corps Department (Rela) personnel assigned to auxiliary rescue and firefighting duties had responded to the blaze without appropriate firefighting PPE.

items.title: Haze watch: 29 areas recording unhealthy or worse air, Larkin, Pasir Gudang API hits 202
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Air quality in Larkin and Pasir Gudang, Johor, deteriorated to very unhealthy levels this evening, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaching 202 as at 5.30pm, while 27 other areas nationwide recorded unhealthy readings. According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, six other areas in Johor recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Pengerang (181), Batu Pahat and Kota Tinggi (171 each), Kluang (168), Tangkak (159) and Segamat (156). Three stations in Negeri Sembilan also recorded unhealthy readings: Nilai (181), Seremban (174) and Port Dickson (170).

items.title: Fatal Senawang crash: Lorry rammed into JPJ car during roadside inspection, police say
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 16 — A lorry carrying dry food products lost control and crashed into a Road Transport Department (JPJ) car and another lorry during a roadside inspection, killing a JPJ officer and injuring three others on the North-South Expressway near Senawang, police said today. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the two JPJ personnel had been inspecting a motoloader carrying a cabin load on the emergency lane at Kilometre 256.1 northbound when the lorry approached from behind at about 10.30pm yesterday. The 42-year-old JPJ officer suffered head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene.

items.title: ‘They were aware’: Bukit Aman on five Malaysians held in Tokyo with cocaine in their shoes
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 16 — Five Malaysians arrested for concealing five kilograms of cocaine in their shoe soles at Haneda International Airport in Tokyo, Japan, on October 10 are believed to have been drug mules paid RM8,000 each. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the suspects, aged between 19 and 26, were each given the shoes by a drug syndicate that is still being identified. He said police were investigating whether all the suspects were directly involved in the syndicate and whether they had previously travelled to other countries using the same modus operandi.

items.title: Wet and windy: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms in 11 states and Putrajaya until 8pm
items.summary: In Kedah, the affected areas include Kubang Pasu, Sik, Baling, Kuala Muda, Langkawi and Padang Terap, while in Perak, the weather alert covers Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Larut, Matang and Selama, Kerian, Kinta, Perak Tengah, Manjung, Hilir Perak and Bagan Datuk. In Kelantan, the warning covers Gua Musang, Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah and Machang, while in Terengganu, it affects Kemaman, Dungun and Hulu Terengganu. In Pahang, the areas involved are Jerantut and Kuantan, while in Selangor, they comprise Petaling, Klang, Kuala Selangor, Kuala Langat, Sepang, Sabak Bernam and Hulu Langat, alongside Tampin in Negeri Sembilan.

items.title: Transport minister vows action if negligence found in Senawang fatal crash involving JPJ officers
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 16 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) will provide full cooperation to the Royal Malaysia Police to ensure that investigations into the accident that claimed the life of one of its personnel at KM256 of the North-South Expressway, near the Senawang exit last night, are conducted thoroughly and transparently. Transport Minister Anthony Loke said appropriate action would be taken against any party found to have violated the law or committed misconduct or negligence, based on the investigation findings. Loke expressed deep sorrow and extended his condolences to the family of Negeri Sembilan JPJ Enforcement Assistant Grade KP2 Mohd Azrul Rashid Yaakub, who was killed in the accident while on duty.

items.title: Want OKU status? Here’s how the Welfare Dept evaluates applications
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 16 — The registration of persons with disabilities (OKU) follows the OKU Registration Guidelines (2019 Amendment), jointly developed by the Social Welfare Department (JKM) and the Health Ministry. In a statement today, JKM said the process also involves medical specialists who sit on the OKU Registration Committee under the National Council for Persons with Disabilities. Medical officers, practitioners or specialists assess an individual’s functionality and disability using the OKU Registration Application Form (BPPOKU Amendment 2/2019), it said.

items.title: Govt overpaid Semantan Estate up to RM500,000 for Duta Enclave land, property valuer tells court
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The High Court was told today that the Malaysian Government had overpaid Semantan Estate Sdn Bhd (1952) between RM400,000 and RM500,000 in compensation for the acquisition of 263.272 acres of land known as the Duta Enclave in 1956. “If the court accepts my valuation, no additional compensation should be paid to the plaintiff (Semantan Estate),” he said. In earlier proceedings, Tan testified that the government paid Semantan Estate RM1.39 million in compensation in 1965, exceeding his recommended amount.

items.title: PeKa B40 becomes PeKa Sihat in healthcare revamp as govt looks to ease clinic queues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Health Ministry’s PeKa B40 healthcare programme will be rebranded as PeKa Sihat, with changes aimed at making the initiative more effective and easing congestion at public health clinics, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. “The Cabinet has agreed to the proposed amendments to the PeKa B40 programme under the Health Ministry, taking into account of its effectiveness in tackling non-communicable diseases. Fahmi said the Health Ministry would announce further details of the rebranded PeKa Sihat programme.

items.title: Italian cyclist targeted by stone-throwing teens while camping in Sabah
items.summary: RANAU, Oct 16 — Police have launched an investigation into a viral video showing a group of teenagers allegedly throwing stones at an Italian cyclist who was camping at Kampung Lohan while on a solo cycling expedition around Sabah. Ranau District Police Chief Supt Mursalin Mahmud said a special team had been formed to investigate the incident after the video attracted public attention. The cyclist, Nicola Chiacchio, had stopped at the Kampung Lohan field during his journey around Sabah using a bicycle.

items.title: Splitting the AG’s two hats: Azalina takes charge of talks with select committee
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Law and Institutional Reform Minister Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said has been tasked with engaging a Parliamentary Special Select Committee on constitutional amendments to separate the roles of the Attorney General and the Public Prosecutor. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim made the announcement after a decree by the Malay Rulers on the proposed amendments at the recent Conference of Rulers meeting, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. “The prime minister has instructed Datuk Seri Azalina to conduct the engagements and discussions with the Parliamentary Special Select Committee, which has already prepared a draft for the constitutional amendments,” Fahmi said at the weekly post-Cabinet media briefing, which was broadcast live.

items.title: Fahmi: No Malaysian palm oil companies involved in burning activities in Indonesia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — There are no Malaysian plantation companies with palm oil concessions in Indonesia that were involved in forest fires linked to the regional haze issue, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said this was based on cross-reference checks conducted with local companies that maintain palm oil concessions in Indonesia. “The Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) will continue to have engagement sessions with Malaysian plantation companies that have their operations in Indonesia,” he said.

items.title: Human Resources Ministry to introduce Starting Basic Salary Guidelines in June 2027 rollout
items.summary: Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the Starting Basic Salary Guidelines based on the Malaysian Standard Classification of Occupations (Masco) would provide more comprehensive starting basic salary benchmarks according to job types and qualification levels. For graduate-level jobs, Ramanan said Kesuma had proposed salary benchmarks for Masco categories 1 to 3, covering graduates with degrees, diplomas and Malaysian Advanced Skills Diplomas at Level 5. “For semi-skilled jobs, Kesuma will align this approach with the Skills-Based Starting Basic Salary Guidelines.

items.title: Pakatan confident of Melaka win, but Amirudin says voters will decide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is confident of winning the upcoming Melaka state election, while acknowledging that the outcome ultimately rests with voters. The coalition’s election director, Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, said PH would announce its candidates for the state election on Oct 24, after he finalises the list with the coalition’s president and top party leaders. Yesterday, PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said discussions on candidates for the Melaka state election were over 95 per cent complete.

items.title: Malaysia unveils six homegrown chips worth RM300m as it shifts from making to designing semiconductors
items.summary: Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Nasir said the six innovations demonstrated the growing capabilities of Malaysian companies, although further work was needed to secure customers, meet industry qualification requirements and turn the designs into commercially successful products. The innovations were developed by companies operating within the Malaysia Semiconductor IC Design Park, with applications ranging from artificial intelligence (AI) and automotive electronics to satellites and autonomous drones. Akmal said Malaysia was building on its established strengths in semiconductor packaging, testing and related manufacturing activities, while expanding into integrated circuit (IC) design through partnerships, talent development and investment.

items.title: Children’s Court closes case of five teenage girls accused of verbally abusing Zara Qairina, submissions set for Nov 16
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 16 — The case involving five teenage girls charged with allegedly uttering abusive words against Zara Qairina Mahathir at the Children’s Court has closed, with submissions scheduled for November 16. Counsel Joan Goh, who represents one of the teenagers, said the court had fixed November 30 for the reply submissions, followed by clarification on December 4 before a date would be set for the ruling on whether a prima facie case had been established. She said more than 20 witnesses had testified during the hearing, but not all child witnesses testified in the Children’s Court and Zara’s mother had also not taken the stand.

items.title: Heavy downpour triggers flash floods across Kuching, roads and Sarawak Plaza basement swamped
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 16 — Several areas in Kuching were hit by flash floods following heavy rain this afternoon. Flooding was reported at Sarawak Plaza, the Mile 3 underpass, Jalan Tun Jugah and Jalan Batu Lintang after the rain began at around 1.30pm. As of 2.45pm, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) had forecast thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several parts of Sarawak until 7pm.

items.title: ‘Until he retracts, go away’: Tuanku Muhriz rebukes Negeri Sembilan MB in public
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, publicly reprimanded Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim as the state’s constitutional crisis drags on. Videos circulating on social media show the ruler telling a group of people that Ismail had written to the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal to say that Tuanku Muhriz was no longer the state’s Yang Dipertuan Besar. A visibly angry Tuanku Muhriz then asked why the menteri besar wanted an audience with him.

items.title: Malaysia’s fury rises as Indonesian haze shuts schools, blankets region, and sparks calls for accountability
items.summary: Indonesian wildfire haze has caused a regional pollution crisis and prompted growing frustration in neighbours, including Malaysia. “Malaysia and Indonesia are close neighbours, but that relationship must also come with responsibility,” Malaysian parliamentarian Syerleena Abdul Rashid told AFP. she said.

items.title: Khazanah and PNB channelled nearly RM40m into FashionValet in 2018, court hears in Vivy Yusof trial
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Sessions Court here was told today that local fashion company, Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd (Fashion Valet), received investment funds totalling nearly RM40 million from Khazanah Nasional Berhad (Khazanah) and Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB) eight years ago. Tay Lay Hong, 54, a banking services manager at the Bukit Damansara branch of Public Bank, said the funds were deposited into a Public Bank account belonging to Fashion Valet through four separate transactions between March and December 2018. Tay also confirmed that a sum of RM11 million was withdrawn from Fashion Valet’s bank account on August 21, 2018, via an online ‘bulk payment’ transaction.

items.title: AAIB releases preliminary report on Long Lellang helicopter crash that killed five
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has published its preliminary report into the September 8 crash of a Flying Doctor Service helicopter at the Long Lellang STOLport in Miri, Sarawak, which killed a pilot and four passengers. The Transport Ministry said the Bolkow BO105 S helicopter, registered 9M-LLF and operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd, was on a scheduled Flying Doctor Service flight from Selungo to the Long Lellang STOLport at the time of the accident. It said the report compiles the factual information identified at the early stage of the investigation, in line with the government’s commitment to transparency and accountability.

items.title: Sarawak gives RM100,000 each to families of Flying Doctor Service crash victims
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 16 — The Sarawak state government has contributed RM100,000 to each of the families of the five victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Baram, which occurred on September 8. Additionally, educational assistance is being provided through Yayasan Sarawak (Sarawak Foundation) to help ease the burden on the victims’ families, specifically by ensuring the continuity of their children’s education. The contributions were presented by Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg to the next-of-kin of the five victims during a handover ceremony held at the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly complex today.
